title: Berserk
label: Quick read (from summaries)
premise: In a dark, medieval-Europe-style fantasy world, the mercenary swordsman Guts joins Griffith's Band of the Hawk and forms deep bonds there. Griffith sacrifices the band to demonic beings to gain godhood, and Guts survives to wage a long war of revenge while protecting the traumatized Casca. Later arcs follow a traveling party seeking healing for her.
life_message: It holds up stubborn endurance against fate and loyalty to the few who stay beside you as what makes life worth living.

content.note: Constant sword and monster combat, dismemberment, torture and mass slaughter (Wikipedia plot; AniList Gore 88%, Torture, Body Horror; CSM on the anime).
Demonic horror, body horror and the 'Eclipse' massacre of the protagonists' comrades (Wikipedia; AniList Tragedy, Demons, Body Horror).
Frequent nudity and a central rape of Casca by Griffith/Femto; other sexual violence and child molestation (Wikipedia; AniList Rape, Nudity; CSM). Shown as atrocity.
Harsh soldiers' profanity per CSM on the anime; manga level (to verify).
Mercenaries drink at times (CSM on the anime; to verify in manga).
Casca is left mentally broken by trauma; Guts's abused childhood and rage; a suicide attempt (Wikipedia; CSM; AniList Tragedy).
Medieval weapons and revenge; hard to imitate, little real-world modeling.
Large franchise with anime and merchandise; no in-story product focus.

delivery.note: Themes of fate and resilience play out through Guts and Griffith, while institutional religion is shown mainly through the fanatic Mozgus and the doubting Farnese.

winners_losers: Ambition that sacrifices others wins worldly power; ordinary comrades are the losers. Sympathy goes to the stubborn survivor and the wounded, while institutional religion appears through a fanatic inquisitor.
